rv.q: This well-crafted, life-opening drama, beautifully directed and performed, has subtly changed us all.

Sarah Frankcom’s atmospheric and absorbing production finds the humanity in these disparate but similarly lost and deluded characters, anchored by strong performances that connect emotionally, despite the heightened artificiality.
Both plays are unflinching observations on the pains and perils of living and of dying yet both are peppered with wry humour and wit that a strong cast delight in.
It is a rewarding one that leaves you with much food for thought.

A presentation of two of Caryl Churchill’s more contemporary plays, Escaped Alone and What If If Only double bill at the Royal Exchange Theatre is a complex yet thrilling theatrical treat that should not be missed.

cn.t: Critics praise Churchill's challenging double bill, with Frankcom's direction drawing strong performances from an experienced cast. The plays showcase Churchill's distinctive fragmented style, political insight, and dark humor to compelling effect.
